newsitem.title: INDIA: Guerrillas kill 22, India army gets special powers.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas kill 22, India army gets special powers.

text.p: The Indian army was granted sweeping shoot-on-sight powers in the northeastern state of Tripura on Sunday after tribal separatist rebels killed 22 people in three remote villages, a government official said.
"The situation is extremely volatile," Tripura's home minister Samar Chowdhury, speaking from the state capital of Agartala, told Reuters in Calcutta by telephone.
"Shoot-at-sight orders have been issued to contain the violence," Chowdhury said.
He said the army and paramilitary reinforcements had also been given powers to arrest and indefinitely detain suspects.

Chowdhury said state authorities had imposed an indefinite curfew in the Khowai region where Sunday's killings of 22 Bengali settlers by separatists belonging to the All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF) occurred.

The guerrillas set ablaze at least 100 homes in the villages of Purbaramachandraghat and Ganda Basti in the western section of the state, then fired on fleeing residents, killing 15 people, police in Agartala said.
A police spokesman said the guerrillas then set fire to a third village, Gorangatilla, where they shot dead seven people.
Sunday's attack was the third in the Khowai area in the past week. Last Sunday tribal separatists set fire to more than 60 houses in ethnic clashes. On Monday they killed 17 people.
"The trouble is still on," the spokesman told Reuters.
"They belong to the ATTF, the modus operandi is the same. They first set fire to houses and when people run out, they open fire on them."
Police and paramilitary troops have launched a search operation for the attackers, he said. The army was patrolling the region to prevent fresh outbreaks of violence.
Security forces had shot dead one rebel since the shoot-on-sight orders were issued, the spokesman said.

"Nobody who will indulge in violence will be spared. We are taking all steps to check violence, to ensure peace, so that life can fast return to normalcy," Chowdhury said. "We have appealed to the people to maintain peace and harmony."
Last July, the ATTF issued a statement warning Bengali settlers to leave the state, which shares an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh.
The state's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy.
More than 2,000 people were killed in the region's worst ethnic riots in June 1980.
